blinding.statement: Neither the draft-stories file nor any wave7-* blind-pass file was opened at any point. Every conclusion below is derived from the extraction files, the recompute report, the source document, the anchor artefacts, and git history.

scope.partition_completeness: These 75 are the COMPLETE MISMATCH set for this document in reports/verification/c4-recompute-report.json (document totals: 122 MATCH, 91 SKIPPED, 75 MISMATCH, 18 UNRESOLVED). This is not a sample.

method.era_determination: Per-CLAIM era via `git blame --line-porcelain HEAD` on the source document, mapping every row's source_lines to the commit that last wrote those lines. Result: 622 of 637 lines blame to c48f639e3 (2026-04-22 08:03 +1000, the audit body); 14 lines to 6b64ad0f6 (2026-05-03 11:24 +1000, the post-recovery banner); 1 line (430) to 044cbcd82 (2026-07-28, the E58 path fix). Of the 75 rows, 74 blame to c48f639e3 and 1 (092#1[0]) to 6b64ad0f6.
method.era_resolution: Each row's anchor+path was resolved from `git show <claim-era-commit>:<anchor>` and compared to the verbatim quote using the harness's OWN comparator, scripts/recompute_c4_claims.py::compare(), imported directly - so the era verdict is produced by the same instrument as the primary verdict, differing only in which commit the anchor is read from.
method.era_result: 75/75 MATCH at the claim's own era (60 mode=exact, 15 mode=round). Zero non-matches. Verified directly by machine for every row - none inferred by pattern.
method.trajectory_reconstruction: Every distinct (anchor, path) pair was additionally resolved at four checkpoints - c48f639e3 (doc era), 6b64ad0f6 (banner era), 8e142df9c^ (immediately before the June re-pricing), and HEAD - to attribute each divergence to a named mover event rather than to 'the artefact moved'.
corroborating_checks: Anchor-path sanity: corrected-f1-multi-buffer/summary.json results[0].R_m == 50 and results[4].R_m == 150 confirmed in both eras - the harness's array indices are correct, not a mis-index.
The cross-file override locator on 093#33[2] was confirmed to have been honoured by the harness (0.799 comes from dawid-skene-results.json, not evaluation.json).
Working-notes re-read at HEAD to test the five cross-reference rows: Obs 256 heading at docs/notes/working-notes.md:11257 and the Obs 273 sentence at :12905 both still carry the quoted figures.
Current cost_manifest.json values re-read from the working tree (200.833 / 30.44 / 207.3382, tiles_failed 0, generated_at 2026-06-12T01:46Z) - the harness's 'actual' column is correct.

instrument_finding.severity: HIGH - affects the era_check field on all 75 rows and, by construction, every multi-edit document in the corpus
instrument_finding.title: era_check resolves at FILE era, not CLAIM era, and therefore collapses to HEAD-era for any document edited after its claims were written
instrument_finding.mechanism: scripts/recompute_c4_claims.py::find_era_commit(doc_path, doc_blob) walks `git log --format=%H -- <doc>` newest-first and returns the first commit whose blob at that path matches the extraction's recorded git_blob. The extraction records the HEAD blob (f76d12a2cd38305eca17d234a8c8d8772737d984), so the 'era commit' resolves to the NEWEST commit that produced the current content - here 044cbcd82 (2026-07-28), a one-line E58 cross-reference fix at line 430 that touched no numeric claim. Every anchor is then read at 2026-07-28, which for artefacts that stopped moving before that date is indistinguishable from HEAD.
instrument_finding.observed_effect: All 75 MISMATCH rows carry era_check {faithful: false, commit: '044cbcd821a8'} and an actual_era essentially equal to the current value. Taken at face value the field says the document was WRONG AT ITS OWN ERA on every one of 75 rows. The truth is the exact opposite: 75/75 were faithful.
instrument_finding.why_it_is_a_trap: This is a single field that, if trusted, converts the entire partition from SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE (ledger-only) to DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA (75 real errors in a results/** document) - the largest possible error in this wave, and one that would land as an unwarranted correction campaign against a historical audit record.
instrument_finding.why_it_was_not_caught_by_the_harness: is_snapshot_doc() fired correctly (dated filename stem), so era_check ran; the defect is downstream of classification, in commit selection. A uniform faithful=false across an entire document is itself the diagnostic signature - a genuinely defective document does not fail era-check on 100 % of its mechanical rows while passing 122 MATCH rows against current artefacts.
instrument_finding.recommended_fix: Resolve era per CLAIM from `git blame` over the claim's source_lines (the blame commit for the line range), not per FILE from the blob. Ruling 14 already licenses this - 'For entry-dated registers ... the snapshot unit is the ENTRY, not the file' - the same principle generalises to any document with a multi-commit authoring history. Where a row's line range spans more than one blame commit, take the newest and record the ambiguity.
instrument_finding.falsifier: Re-run era_check with commit=c48f639e3 (or per-line blame) and every one of the 75 rows flips to faithful=true. I did exactly this using the harness's own compare() function.

verdict_counts_note: INSTRUMENT is recorded as 0 at ROW level deliberately: the harness's primary resolution (anchor, path, current value) is correct on all 75, so no row's MISMATCH status is an artefact of the instrument. The instrument defect is in the supplementary era_check field and is reported above at programme level rather than smeared across 75 row verdicts. Every row also carries harness_era_check_wrong:true so the finding is not lost per-row.

causal_account.one_line: Nothing is wrong with this document's numbers: all 75 figures were exact-or-correctly-rounded transcriptions of their cited artefacts on 2026-04-22 (and 2026-05-03 for the banner), and the artefacts were subsequently rewritten out from under them by three dated, named, deliberate campaigns - so the partition is 70 SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE plus 5 rows the extractor mis-anchored, and zero defects.
causal_account.long_form: This document is a dated audit report whose §A tables transcribe seven artefacts field-by-field with explicit JSON key paths. Between its authoring era and today those artefacts moved three times: (E1) the 2026-05-02/03 recovery campaign, which recovered 160 failed text-high tile-passes, re-evaluated all three runs against the reviewed ground truth of 4,745 features, and re-aggregated Dawid-Skene - this moved every F1/precision/recall/D-S row and the multi-buffer, cross-tab and gold-standard-subtype rows; (E2) commit 8e142df9c on 2026-06-12, which regenerated all four 55-map cost manifests at audited flex pricing, removing a 2-3x recovery-merge inflation and reconstructing stub verifier legs - this moved every cost, token, wall-clock and tile-count row, and moved them further than E1 had; and (E3) commits 3271d6923 / 30a902f56 on 2026-08-03, the W6-E8/W6-E9 corrected-F1 regeneration, which moved the two multi-buffer rows a third time DURING this verification programme. The document itself already tracks E1 in part: its 2026-05-03 banner correctly declared §A4 superseded and correctly recorded the then-current post-recovery figures. What it cannot track is E2 and E3, which post-date every edit to it. The apparent mass failure is therefore an artefact of comparing an as-of-2026-04-22 record against a 2026-08-04 tree - amplified by an era_check that was itself reading the 2026-08-04 tree.
falsifiable_predictions: P1. Resolving any of the 74 body rows at c48f639e3, or 092#1[0] at 6b64ad0f6, yields MATCH under the harness's own compare(). FALSIFIED IF any row fails. (Tested: 75/75 MATCH.)

P2. Every cost-family row's final move is attributable to 8e142df9c and its value at 8e142df9c^ differs from both the era value and the current value. FALSIFIED IF any cost row's current value already held before 8e142df9c. (Tested: holds for all 22 cost-manifest rows except the four tiles_failed/failure_rate values, which reached 0 at E1 for text-high and at E2 for text-min - recorded per row.)

P3. No row in this partition is a fabrication or a transcription slip: every quoted digit string is reproducible from a git blob. FALSIFIED IF any row's era value differs from the quote at the quoted precision. (Tested: none does.)

P4. The five EXTRACTION-DEFECT rows will still verify against docs/notes/working-notes.md at any future date, because working notes are append-only under charter §2 / §10 item 2. FALSIFIED IF an Obs is ever edited in place.
P5. If the era_check bug is fixed (per-claim blame) and the recompute re-run, the number of DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA rows for this document is 0. FALSIFIED IF any row is wrong at its own era.

materiality.the_document_level_finding: The 20 material rows are not scattered - they are the cost/token/wall-clock/tile-failure block, and together they invert an ordering. At its era this document supports 'text HIGH costs ~1/5 of image' ($69.60 vs $364.70). The audited flex-priced manifests give $207.34 vs $200.83 - a 0.97x ratio, i.e. approximately equal API cost, which is precisely the correction ruling 16 / escalation W6-E1 already made against the cross-track report's '2.9x lower API cost' claim. This document is another upstream carrier of that superseded ordering and should be named in the same family.

It carries no extractable number and will be missed by a numeric sweep.

Line 616-618 §G item 1 and line 621-624 §G item 3 carry the $60.79 and $69.60 figures inside a 'what changed relative to the 2026-04-18 audit' narrative - these are 093#41[1] and 093#43[3] and are era-faithful, but the surrounding narrative reads as a correction record and will mislead a reader who does not reach the banner.
materiality.sibling_document_coupling: Ruling 17's closing sentence (P2 R9 coupling discipline) applies across the directory, not just within this file. The same superseded figures live in three siblings, all outside this pass's row set: results/documentation-audit/README.md:17 ('cost $126.81'); results/documentation-audit/audit-summary.md:17,20-21 ('$69.60 -> $126.81' and 'should be read as $552.30 post-recovery ($364.70 image + $60.79 text-MIN + $126.81 text-HIGH)' - the audited three-run total is $438.61 = 200.833 + 30.44 + 207.3382); results/documentation-audit/verification-2026-04-21.md:19 ('totals.cost_usd: 126.8051'), whose C09/C45/C74/U06 rows also record PASS verdicts against the superseded manifest. Repairing this file alone leaves three documents asserting the old numbers.

document_classification.ruling: DATED SNAPSHOT for its measurement content; IN Document-Revision-Policy scope for its apparatus and its pointers.
document_classification.repair_implication: Banner/rider, not an in-place refresh of the §A1/§A3/§A4 tables. Concretely: (1) extend and correct the existing 2026-05-03 banner with a dated 2026-08-04 rider that covers §A1 and §A3 as well as §A4, corrects its own $126.81 to the audited $207.34, and names the two campaigns (E2 re-pricing, E3 corrected-F1); (2) attach the Document Revision Policy apparatus - 'Last revised' line plus a `## Changelog` section - because the document IS an anchor doc in scope and back-fill-on-touch now applies; (3) leave every §A table cell as written; (4) fix broken POINTERS in place, following the 044cbcd82 precedent.
evidence_for_snapshot: Line 3 scopes the document's own truth-claim to a repository state: '**Audit period**: repository state through commit `2165013c`'. A self-declared as-of commit bound is the strongest possible snapshot signal and outranks directory location.
Dated title ('Full Run-by-Run Table (2026-04-22)') and dated filename - the ruling-12/14 presentation class, advisory but concordant.

Genre: it is the RECORD OF AN AUDIT. It exists because the prior 2026-04-19 audit carried hallucinated cost figures (README.md 'Supersedes'). Rewriting its numbers destroys the only evidence of what the corrected audit actually verified - ruling 1's stated rationale ('in-place correction would falsify the record of what the session actually found') applies with full force, and it is a C6 attestation source.

Revealed practice: on 2026-05-03 the maintainer had the chance to edit and deliberately did not. Commit 6b64ad0f6 describes the change as 'light annotation noting §A4 cells cite pre-recovery state' and applied the same annotation-not-edit treatment to all four documents in the directory.
The banner's own wording is snapshot semantics: 'Those values remain accurate for the original launch snapshot but have been superseded by...'
§G is a diff against the 2026-04-18 audit - a section that is only coherent in its own era.

In-repo precedent for exactly this call: docs/methodology/output-directory-standard.md's 2026-08-02 changelog records that era-exact dated censuses were 'verified era-exact and are deliberately unchanged (snapshot statements ...)' even inside a living document.
evidence_for_living: planning/documentation-audit-plan.md § 5.2 lists 'results/documentation-audit/*.md (4 docs)' as an anchor-doc class - so it is inside the `results/**.md` Revision-Policy row of docs/methodology/output-directory-standard.md's scope table (which reads 'anchor docs only - see audit plan § 5.2'). Its assessed compliance there is 'Compliant - Self-aware; banner present', i.e. the banner IS how this document is expected to comply.

It has been edited in place once: 044cbcd82 (2026-07-28) fixed the §B3 working-notes path. But even that edit preserved the record rather than overwriting it - it kept the old citation visible ('the path cited here previously, ... does not exist') instead of silently substituting the new one.
document_classification.the_operative_rule: The repo has, in practice, been running a coherent split that ruling 17 does not yet spell out: in a dated snapshot that is also an anchor doc, POINTERS ARE LIVING AND MEASUREMENTS ARE SNAPSHOT. Paths, cross-references, Obs line numbers, supersession banners and changelogs are apparatus - they are maintained in place because their whole job is to be current. Measured values are findings - they are frozen and superseded by rider. Both the 2026-05-03 and the 2026-07-28 edits obey this rule; so does the ruling-14 precedent in output-directory-standard.md. I recommend the PI ratify it explicitly, because 'results/**.md is in Revision-Policy scope' and 'dated snapshots keep ruling-1 treatment' otherwise read as a direct contradiction on this exact file.
document_classification.how_to_falsify_this_ruling: If the PI rules that anchor-doc status alone forces in-place refresh, then §A1/§A3/§A4 must be rewritten to 200.833 / 30.44 / 207.3382 and the F1 tables to the post-recovery values. The test of whether that is right: after such a rewrite, can anyone still answer 'what did the 2026-04-21 re-audit actually find, and was it correct?' The answer is no - and that question is the document's entire reason for existing, since it was itself commissioned to replace an audit that had invented figures.
document_classification.note_on_ruling_14: Ruling 14's 'presentation class is ADVISORY ONLY' governs the per-claim TRIAGE disposition, and I have honoured it: the dated filename played no part in any row verdict - all 75 were decided by machine era-resolution. The snapshot-vs-living question answered here is the ruling-17 REPAIR-layer question, which is a document-class question and is decided on the evidence above, not on the filename.
